newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-WOMEN'S GROUP DEMANDS IOC SANCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-WOMEN'S GROUP DEMANDS IOC SANCTIONS.

text.p: A women's group called on the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Friday to apply the same sanctions against countries that discriminate against women in sport as were imposed on apartheid South Africa.

The Atlanta/Sydney Plus Group, organised to pressure the IOC to end discrimination in the Olympic movement on basis of sex, is in Geneva to take its cause to the United Nations Human Rights Commission, now holding its annual six-week session.
A spokesman for the group told a news conference the IOC, based in the Swiss city of Lausanne, was violating its own charter by not acting.

"The Olympics are ruled only by the Olympic charter which excludes any form of discrimination," said the spokeswoman, Linda Weil-Curiel of France. "If countries don't want to compete then they shouldn't send anyone -- men or women.
"Why should men be allowed to participate when women aren't? This is what we ask the IOC, to be courageous and take a stand," she added. "Are women worth less than the South African blacks?"
For over three decades South Africa was kept isolated from international sports competition and out of the Olympics because of its apartheid policies.
The Atlanta/Sydney Group, which claims the support of the European parliament, would like to see similar bans imposed against countries that do not allow women to compete in the Olympics.
According to the group's statistics, 25 countries at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, the majority from Africa and Asia, practised discrimination on the basis of sex by sending all-male delegations.
At the 1994 Barcelona Olympics, 35 nations sent all-male teams. Weil-Curiel said she believed the drop was the result of pressure applied by her group.

"I really think it was because the pressure we made that countries like Pakistan and Iran sent one woman each to Atlanta," she said. "Now we must maintain the pressure for the 2000 Olympics in Sydney.
According to figures presented by the Group to the news conference, the following sent no women to Atlanta:
Africa -- Botswana, Djibouti, Guinea-Bissau, Libya, Mauritania, Rwanda, Senegal, Somalia, Sudan, Togo.
Middle East and Asia -- Afghanistan, Brunei, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Yemen.
